results.title: [PDF] an empirical investigation of factors influencing the adoption and ...
results.content: Although there is current literature on the correlation between perceived ease of use and attitudes toward tech-nology adoption in agriculture, there is still a significant study vacuum in understanding the specific elements that influence the adoption of smart fertilizer technology. By building upon the principles of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), which suggests that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions all impact the behavioral intention to adopt technology [108], it is needed to conduct an additional study into the correla-tion between social influence and perceived trust within the agricultural domain. The current research, which centers on smart fertilizer technology in the agricultural sector, incorporated perceived cost as a moderating factor to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the interplay between perceived trust, non-adoption intention, and adoption intention. Expanding on this, the subsequent hypothesis is developed: In the context of smart fertilizer technology in the agriculture sector, the relationship between perceived trust and adoption inten-tion, as well as non-adoption intention, is moderated by perceived cost.
